description: Every port either role listens on or dials. Overlay-only ports are unreachable from the WAN by design. `ports` is the fabric namespace (peer/master listeners); `node_ports` is the spark-node compose stack (docker host-publishes and in-stack listeners), recorded separately because the two namespaces share numbers without sharing sockets.
invariants: No role binds a wildcard address for an overlay-only port.
Peer-side listeners that inject local identity or accept mutations stay off the overlay.
The Master binds 9090 nowhere; it dials peers on 9090.
implementation_state never claims implemented without a bind path in the named service.

A port may be implemented and simultaneously not-listening. That combination is the normal case for an overlay service on a host whose overlay is down, and it must not be collapsed into a single boolean.
runtime is measured per host and never published as a contract fact; only implementation_state travels.

A service built on the shared transport (shared/sparknet-http.py) may declare a route class loopback-only via serve(loopback_only_routes=...). A caller from the overlay is then refused HTTP 403 before the request is read — a signed and authorized peer included. Overlay-only ports must never expose such a route class to the fabric.

Re-formation news uses no new port: the chained lineage is pulled over the existing share/registry path (4220 git-repo or 4201 share-intake), the same channel the receiving peer already grants. Adding a port would hand re-formation a transport edge no other authority has.

Node ports and fabric ports share a NUMBER space but not a socket. A `node_ports` number that also appears in `ports` is a documentation signal, not a conflict: the node publishes to the docker host namespace (loopback by default for anything not meant to be a LAN API), the fabric listens in the overlay namespace. A same-host deployment must keep the node default off any address a fabric listener needs.

A node port that is not host-published (host_published: false) is reachable only to its own stack on the docker network, and is `not-verifiable-here` rather than `not-listening` precisely because there is nothing on the host to observe — the distinction is the code's, not a measurement's.

The node's only fabric-facing number is the agent gateway (8080). Host-published engine, bus, compute and admin numbers are appliances, not fabric edges: joining a fabric changes where the agent's authority comes from, not which ports the node exposes.

The knowledge services (ingest, backup) listen on no port: ingest is a one-shot indexer and backup writes signed snapshots to a directory, so neither belongs in this table. They are node services in spark.compose.yml, contracted by their profiles, and absence from `node_ports` is the statement that they open no socket.

measurement.caveat: Runtime states are true of THIS host only. A port marked not-listening here may be running on a node with a live overlay. implementation_state is a property of the code and travels with the contract; runtime is a property of one machine and does not.
measurement.host: single peer, aarch64, no WireGuard kernel interface available
measurement.method: ss -ltnup, plus reading each named service's bind path

node_measurement.caveat: The node's numbers live in the docker host-publish namespace, not the overlay namespace, so a shared NUMBER with a fabric port is not by itself a collision — the ADDRESS decides. On this host specifically, 4222/8222/8000 are currently held by the raxxar Aegis cluster (its nats-server and orchestrator), so a node bring-up here needs an override for those three; that is a property of this machine, recorded because it is the most common first surprise, not a contract fact.
node_measurement.host: the development host, compose graph NOT running
node_measurement.method: reading every `ports:` mapping in spark.compose.yml, plus ss on this host

4110.note: The Go typed-memory service (sparknet-memory). Loopback only: the Python gateway is the authority front door and the service trusts only that gateway token. It holds no key, signs no note and writes no vault page. The gateway runs in the node image on the host network at 127.0.0.1:4093 and opens no published compose port.

4200.collision_note: The number is the same and the meaning is nearly the same, but the namespaces differ: the fabric entry describes a role's systemd server (still unbuilt and, per its test, spec-only), this one the node image's compose service. Only one is ever brought up; the loopback bind keeps either clear of the other.
4200.note: The node's opencode server over the vault (spark-entrypoint opencode). Loopback only: it carries the whole node's session authority, so it is never a fabric edge despite the number. OpenCode v2 requires HTTP basic auth, so this opt-in profile refuses to start without OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD; the 4204 engine is the supported user surface. Sessions and caches are pointed into the mounted state so they survive a container recreation.
4200.runtime_why: The compose stack is not running on this host; the ports: mapping exists in spark.compose.yml and is the bind path (the opencode profile is opt-in).

4096.note: OpenAI-compatible local proxy routing to domain agent ports. The OpenAI/session/vault route class is local-only by design: it injects the user environment profile, so it stays loopback-only even when the bridge is bound to the overlay (`LOCAL_ONLY_PREFIXES`; an overlay source is refused `403 not-loopback` before the request is read). The `/admin/*` route is the implemented Master-signed exception and the only route class the overlay may reach. The `/sandbox/*` name is reserved for peer PLAN 20E; no handler exists and it is not overlay-reachable today.

Requests are signed with the node's own key from .state/keys; unsigned or stale traffic is refused with a JSON 401. The bridge's bind path is asserted end to end by tests/test_http_transport.py against a real loopback socket, but no daemon holds 4096 open on the development host, and none should be — `implemented` + `not-listening` is the honest pair: the code exists and binds when invoked.

4201.binds_to: the peer's own overlay address only
4201.note: Receives share offers and countersigned share grants from a sibling peer. It also carries the proposal-exchange message family (proposal.submit/review/decision, contracts/proposal-schema.json `transport`) — a route on this port, not a new port and not a share type, because a proposal conveys no knowledge read or copy. Overlay-only because every request here must arrive over the fabric, carrying a grant naming the sender's fingerprint.

On the live pair 2026-10-31, sparknet-share-serve.service bound this port on 10.100.0.2 (peer sparknet-node-0001) and 10.100.0.1 (master sparknet-node-0002); both listeners verify a signed envelope and use a 0600 Unix socket for local control. The `runtime` axis describes this host, so it stays not-listening; `status` records the live pair.

4201.transport_personality: Peer personality only: the shared transport (shared/sparknet-http.py) classifies the caller by source address, and a loopback-only route class is refused 403 before the request is read. The share stanza has no local face; only a sibling on the overlay may dial it.

4202.note: Carries a handoff payload. Separate from share-intake so that granting conversation passing does not implicitly grant knowledge sharing: two ports, two independent grants. The proposal-exchange family is reachable on either share port (contracts/proposal-schema.json `transport.ports`), since a proposal is not a share type and is not gated by the knowledge/conversation split.

4210.note: Vote exchange for a master election. Carries signed votes only — never a registry entry and never an approval, so it is not an authority-plane message even though it decides who holds the operational key. Distinct from 4203 share-ratification so that electing a master and confirming a share stay separately gated.

4211.binds_to: the peer's own overlay address only
4211.note: The non-serving probe port for peer liveness. The listener accepts a TCP connection and closes it without reading or writing a byte, so a monitor can ask whether a sibling's address exists without making any serving path do work. It is overlay-only and peer-bound; nothing here carries a request, a claim or an authority message. A liveness claim travels the other way, as a `kind=liveness` telemetry report to the Master's 8090 intake (contracts/health-protocol.md, contracts/telemetry-schema.json).
4211.runtime_why: peer-node/services/sparknet-liveness-monitor.py binds this port (default 4211; --port moves it only for a loopback test or a same-host collision) and peer-node/systemd/sparknet-liveness-monitor.service runs it, but this host has no WireGuard interface, so the peer's overlay address cannot be bound or observed. The service is installed by the peer's unit installer and enabled by the operator; on a host without an overlay it declines rather than binding a wildcard.
4211.status: IMPLEMENTED, NOT RUNNING HERE — the probe listener is peer-node/services/sparknet-liveness-monitor.py; the shared state machine is shared/sparknet-liveness.py. Probe targets come from the Master-signed registry and are signature-checked. The live cross-node leg is `DoD: confirm: user` in fabric Step 70D.

8090.note: The Master's peer→Master intake listener. RE-SCOPED by fabric Step 69C from the superseded master-instant-push: Step 6 pushes the signed registry Master→peer on 9090, so the old ACL-push purpose was retired, and Master Step 7's open 'survives / re-scoped / retired' question is answered — re-scoped. It carries peer→Master message families as routes, exactly as the peer's guard 9090 carries three: POST /api/v1/telemetry (overlay-attributed evidence push, contracts/telemetry-schema.json) and, from fabric Step 70B, POST /api/v1/rfi-request (contracts/rfi-schema.json) and, from Step 91, POST /api/v1/issues (contracts/issue-schema.json). Attribution is the authenticated overlay — a body is matched to the fingerprint the Master's registry maps its source address to. The telemetry route enforces the peer-held `telemetry` capability on receipt; the request route requires only a registered, non-revoked peer, because asking a question is not reporting evidence. It carries no authority: it records evidence, acknowledges and queues requests for the composer.
8090.runtime_why: master-node/services/sparknet-peer-intake.py implements the listener (telemetry + RFI requests) and master-node/systemd/sparknet-peer-intake.service stages it, but this host has no WireGuard interface, so 10.100.0.1 cannot be observed. The unit is staged, not enabled — enabling a peer-facing socket on the authority-plane node is an operator decision, as with the signer and reflex broker units.

9090.binds_to: the peer's own overlay address only
9090.note: The guard binds 10.100.0.x, never 0.0.0.0. That is why a legitimate Master request arrives from 10.100.0.1 and off-overlay clients are rejected. Three routes share this port: POST /api/v1/critical-file/patch (guard approval, contracts/guard-approval.json), POST /api/v1/registry (signed registry publication, contracts/registry-publication.json) and POST /api/v1/rfi (signed RFI answer into 01_Inbox, contracts/rfi-schema.json). All three are push-only, source-gated to loopback and the Master overlay address, and self-authenticating: a third route adds no transport edge and no new attack surface.
9090.runtime_why: The daemon refuses to listen without an overlay address (peer-node/services/sparknet-guard-d.py:709-711, standalone mode). With wg0 absent it correctly declines to bind rather than falling back to a wildcard. This is the code working, not code missing — the distinction the previous boolean could not express.

11501.note: Base of the per-user OpenShell model-proxy range (`proxy_port` plus allocator index). Loopback only; the VM guest reaches its proxy as host.openshell.internal:<port>. The range stops before the forward range.
11501.runtime_why: The engine binds one loopback proxy per active sandbox; no sandbox is running on this host at measurement time.

14201.note: Base of the per-user OpenShell forward range (`forward_base` plus allocator index). `openshell forward service` maps each loopback port to the VM's OpenCode 4200 and preserves Basic auth.
14201.runtime_why: The engine starts one loopback forward per active VM sandbox; none is running on this host at measurement time.

17670.note: The OpenShell gateway control plane. Loopback only, package-managed mTLS; it is never exposed to the overlay and carries no knowledge. The peer's engine is the only client.
17670.runtime_why: The package user service binds 127.0.0.1:17670 when installed and running; it is stopped on this measurement host.
